item.research_question: How do point defect clusters in high-temperature superconductors lead to the formation of ferromagnetic clusters embedded within the superconductor?
item.material_system: YBa2Cu3O7-δ (Y123) thin films with Y124 intergrowths
item.processing_route: Chemical Solution Deposition (CSD) with pyrolysis and crystallization steps
item.test_conditions: Temperature range: 1.6-100 K, magnetic field range: -6 to 6 T
key_findings: Cu di-vacancies decorated by three O vacancies (2V Cu+3V O) are the most stable type of Cu defect
The four Cu atoms neighboring the defect carry a total moment of 1.3 μB per defect
The magnetic moments of the Cu atoms in the double chain and in the CuO2 planes in the vicinity of the defects are of the same sign, i.e., ferromagnetically coupled
The system behaves like a superparamagnet, with a Curie dependence of the effective spin moment with temperature
The field dependence of the total magnetization can be well fitted by the Langevin function, indicating superparamagnetic behavior of isolated ferromagnetic clusters
item.mechanism: The ferromagnetic order of the Cu atoms in the superconducting Y123 films is explained in terms of a superparamagnetic behavior of isolated ferromagnetic clusters, even below the superconducting transition temperature
item.limitations: The restriction on the size of the supercells that can be used in DFT calculations limits the ability to comment on long-range magnetic ordering
item.future_work: Investigating the role of the novel ferromagnetic behavior in pinning vortices, and searching for the presence of magnetism in the vicinity of superconductivity in other defective perovskite-based systems
quotes: the ferromagnetic order of those Cu belonging to the CuO2 planes and surrounding the O-decorated Cu vacancies does not vanish when superconductivity sets in at T c

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do point defect clusters in high-temperature superconductors lead to the formation of ferromagnetic clusters embedded within the superconductor?. System: YBa2Cu3O7-δ (Y123) thin films with Y124 intergrowths. Processing: Chemical Solution Deposition (CSD) with pyrolysis and crystallization steps. Test conditions: Temperature range: 1.6-100 K, magnetic field range: -6 to 6 T. Findings: Cu di-vacancies decorated by three O vacancies (2V Cu+3V O) are the most stable type of Cu defect; The four Cu atoms neighboring the defect carry a total moment of 1.3 μB per defect; The magnetic moments of the Cu atoms in the double chain and in the CuO2 planes in the vicinity of the defects are of the same sign, i.e., ferromagnetically coupled; The system behaves like a superparamagnet, with a Curie dependence of the effective spin moment with temperature; The field dependence of the total magnetization can be well fitted by the Langevin function, indicating superparamagnetic behavior of isolated ferromagnetic clusters. Mechanism: The ferromagnetic order of the Cu atoms in the superconducting Y123 films is explained in terms of a superparamagnetic behavior of isolated ferromagnetic clusters, even below the superconducting transition temperature. Limitations: The restriction on the size of the supercells that can be used in DFT calculations limits the ability to comment on long-range magnetic ordering. Future work: Investigating the role of the novel ferromagnetic behavior in pinning vortices, and searching for the presence of magnetism in the vicinity of superconductivity in other defective perovskite-based systems.
